resources.string: One phone becomes the screen. The other becomes the hands.
Captures this screen with MediaProjection, encodes it to H.264 and serves it over WiFi. The system will ask you to confirm screen capture.
Finds hosts on the same network with mDNS (or an IP you type), decodes the H.264 stream and draws it full screen.
Unavailable on this phone: screen capture needs Android 5.0 (API 21), and this device runs Android %1$s. Its working role is the guest - it can find another phone and control it.
Note: on Android 5.0-6.x this phone can mirror its screen but cannot be touched - gesture injection needs Android 7.0. To control a phone from this one, use the guest role.
Milestone 1: mirroring over WiFi. TCP port %1$d, %2$d-byte frame header, H.264 payload. Touch injection lands in milestone 2.
No WiFi address yet — are you connected to a network or hotspot?
Android shows a system dialog asking you to confirm screen capture. The stream keeps running when you leave this screen - stop it from the notification.
Open Guest mode on this phone
Only useful for a loopback smoke test: you cannot watch this phone\'s own screen on it, because opening Guest mode hides the Host screen you are mirroring.
Notification permission denied - the mirroring notification will be hidden, but the stream still works
No hosts found yet. Make sure the host is mirroring and both phones are on the same WiFi, or type the IP shown on the host.
That does not look like an IP address
Lets a paired guest phone tap and scroll on this screen

GhostHand replays touches that arrive from a guest phone you connected (over WiFi) onto this screen, so the guest can tap and scroll here. Nothing is recorded and no screen content is read: this service only performs gestures.
Enabled — guests can tap and scroll
Disabled — the guest can watch but not touch
Android only lets an accessibility service inject touches. Enable GhostHand touch control once and it stays on; you can switch it off in the same place.
Tap and drag on the guest to control this phone. Drags land when the finger lifts.
This phone runs Android %1$s. Gesture injection arrived in Android 7.0, so this phone can mirror but cannot be controlled. The guest side works on any host.
Shown while GhostHand is capturing and serving this screen
A hand taps the screen, and the glass ripples
